newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Jail terms sought for S.Korean campus protesters.
newsitem.headline: Jail terms sought for S.Korean campus protesters.

text.p: South Korean prosecutors sought prison terms for about 50 of 62 university students who went on trial on Tuesday in connection with violent campus demonstrations in August, court officials said.
State prosecutors in Seoul District Court demanded about 50 defendants serve two to six years in jail for their roles in the protests at Seoul's Yonsei University, the officials said.
"Most of the students acknowledged their involvement in the demonstration," one court official told Reuters.

The charges ranged from acts of violence, such as wielding steel pipes against police and throwing fire bombs, to interference in police duties and violating the National Security Law, officials said.

More than 3,200 students were arrested in August after riot police stormed the campus to end seven days of occupation by the students. The protesters were demanding reunification with North Korea and the withdrawal of U.S. troops stationed in the South.

Most of the students in court on Tuesday pleaded for leniency, arguing that they aimed to promote unification of the Korean peninsula. Prosecutors said their goals amounted to a breach of national security by supporting North Korea.
North and South Korea technically remain at war after the 1950-53 Korean War ended in a ceasefire rather than a peace pact.
A total of 444 students have been charged in connection with the protests -- the worst since President Kim Young-sam took power in February 1993.

Thirty-eight students face charges under the National Security law, which bars all unapproved contacts with North Korea, while 10 have been charged in connection with the murder of a policeman who died of head wounds during the protests.
The remaining students face charges over their involvement in the demonstrations.
Of the 444 students, 241 are being tried at Seoul District Court. The others are being handled at its four branches.
Three groups of students will be tried per day on Tuesdays and Fridays through to the end of the month. Sentences were expected to be announced from October 29.
